newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to delay economic deregulation package.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to delay economic deregulation package.

text.p: Indonesia has delayed the launch of its latest package of economic deregulation measures to early next month from June because of last month's general elections, the Harian Ekonomi Neraca newspaper reported on Friday.

Saleh Afiff, the Coordinating Minister for Economics, Finance and Supervisor of Development, was quoted as saying the delay was also due to trade missions in June by Industry and Trade Minister Tunky Ariwibowo to Poland, Hungary and Romania.
He was also quoted as saying there were differences of opinions among ministers involved in drawing up the package, but added that they were "usual".
Government officials were not immediately available for comment.

The Indonesian government routinely unveils measures aimed at bolstering economic growth ahead of the meeting of the Consultative Group on Indonesia (CGI), a grouping of donor nations and financial institutions led by the World Bank.
Indonesia expects to obtain some $5 billion in aid this year from the CGI, which meets in Japan next month. The CGI pledged $5.26 billion last year, compared with $5.35 billion in 1995.
The World Bank said on Wednesday it recommended CGI aid to Indonesia in 1997 be maintained at the 1996 level.
"Total 1997 CGI commitments similar to last year's would be very supportive," the Bank said in its annual report on Indonesia's economy.
It said also that Indonesia's deregulation programme was losing momentum and that this could affect the health of the economy.
